**Introduction** 

It’s not as bad as you think. 

Hi everyone, my name is LaToya Gay and I have been a stay/work at home mother almost 4 years now. I have worked in the corporate world since I was 16 and although I learned a lot and gained the knowledge that helped me start my own business I desired more. I desired to be at home with my children when they got home from school. I desired to have dinner ready once my hubby walked in the door from a long day at work. I wanted more for my family and I was determined to make it happen\! I knew that God had something prepared for me but I was fearful of moving forward and my actions grew stagnant. 

There were many times where I appeared to be all over the place and trying different things because I was not clear of my purpose. I surrounded myself around people that I thought were for me but realized that in the end they were only there for a season and had to be released immediately afterwards. I did not have the faith in God that I should have to walk towards my destiny boldly and unashamed. With me now being 29 years old (yes, it took that long\!) I finally realized how important my purpose really is and through much prayer and meditation God revealed to me the desires of my heart. 

For years I went from job to job, college to college unaware that I was not being the role model that my children needed to see from mommy. I was not being consistent, stable or proactive in anything that I did. It seemed 

like I would start something and then after a few months I would get tired of doing it and start something else. That is not the way to go about life and that is not how you want to live your life. You have to pray and write down your vision and allow God to give you the direction that you need to move forward\! 

By the end of 2012, God had not only revealed to me the name of my business but he also showed me things and people that had to be removed out of my life in order for me to be successful and remain focused. I know you may be wondering why I am sharing all of this with you or you may be  
receiving the confirmation that you have been praying for to help you walk forward boldly and be the entrepreneur that God has called you to be\! Being inconsistent, unstable, lazy, confused, and whatever else that is not of God is not the direction for your life. 

I was determined to start 2013 on a stable mind and become more consistent and that is how VirtuallyNSync, LLC was birthed. 

I absolutely love what I do and I have a passion to help people like you find work at home opportunities that best suits your goals and/or dreams. Now this guide is not going to be the typical boring work at home manual that leaves you wondering what next at the end. To be honest it is not as bad as you think\! You are probably at the point where you want to give up but I am going to help you get started, teach you how to stand out from the rest and show you the best places to look but you have to be ready to get started\! 

You have to be willing to put in the work and be prepared to walk in success and oh providing a recommendation for my services won’t hurt either. We are going to have fun going through this guide together so make sure to bring out your pen and paper and take notes because this journey is going to be an awesome ride\! Now go ahead and turn the page because I know you are excited to read what happens next, right?\!  
**Chapter 1** 

**Starting from Scratch** 

**![][image2]**  
So you want to work from home and/or start your own business\! Maybe you are preparing to leave the corporate world for good and be home with your children, spend more time with your family. Whatever the case may be, you are clueless as to where to start and need help getting motivated and want some assistance with the process. That is where this guide comes in. I am not going to just show you how to get started but I will also help guide you through the process of knowing where to look and how to avoid falling for the same scams and junk that I did\! 

The first thing that I would encourage you to do is stop bringing out your wallet every time you see a so-called employer trying to charge hundreds of dollars for a position that does not even give you a detailed description of what they require from you. That way you are not wasting your money, you are not losing money and you are using your discernment effectively. I can remember the many times I paid for these so called scams and tried to fight and get my money back but it always led to a dead end. I am going to help you stop seeing that dead end and find legit work at home opportunities that are real, relevant and a lot of times free to apply\! I don’t know about you but when your pockets are empty because you have spent it all on scams I  
think you are more than happy to say, “Yes, I love free for once.” (This is where you smile) J 

When we think of starting from scratch you think starting over, picking up the pieces and trying to make sense of what is about to transpire. You have already wasted too much of your hard earned money so now what? Well, I want you to start thinking about what you love to do. 

· Write down your strongest points and your desires and allow God to reveal to you the desires of your heart. The last thing you want to do is look for a position that you know in your heart that you will hate doing. 

· Do not search for work at home opportunities just because it gives you something to do. Search because your desire to be at home with your family more often is necessary. Search because your vision is greater than your life. While you are reading this guide I want you to keep in mind that not every application that you send out to the employers and/or companies are going to be sent back to you with a yes. There will be many rejections but what I want you to realize is that if your desire is greater than the fear of rejection than you will continue to press forward and not give up and start over from scratch. 

· Have faith in yourself. Encourage yourself so that once you start on your journey you will be ready, prepared and confident that you are going to come out of this process successful and ready for business.  
**Chapter 2** 

How do I set up my home office? 

![][image3]  
In this chapter we are going to help you get your home office set up and prepare for your first assignment\! You have to be mindful that your home office should resemble that of the corporate office. You do not want to have any distractions around you. Here are the steps that you need to ensure a distraction-free and organized work environment. 

1\. Be sure that you have a space that is dedicated specifically for your work environment. 

2\. Have a desk, a nice sized desk, where you can place your desktop or laptop and still have space for your paperwork and writing area, and a comfortable chair. 

3\. Make sure your desk is free of clutter. You want to make sure that anything that is not work related is removed from your office.  
4\. You want to have a dedicated phone line just for business purposes. No call waiting, voicemail, just the basic phone line, and have the high speed connection. VOIP is not allowed, and magic jack is not allowed, it needs to have a landline 

5\. It is helpful to have a multi-function printer just in case you need to send a fax or scan and email a document back to an employer. 

6\. You want to make sure your office space is in a well-ventilated area. Using a fan may be heard by the customer on the call. Be mindful-- customers do not know you are working from home. Let’s keep it that way and be professional at all times. 

Now that you have all these things you are closer to your journey from working from home. The steps that I have provided you may not be all the steps a employer requires but these are the basic steps so that you are able to make it an easy transition into your work at home journey.  
**Chapter 3** 

To Be or Not To Be: Employee or Independent Contractor? 

![][image4]  
A lot of my clients have asked me: what is the difference between an employee and an independent contractor? So I’ve decided to give a little insight so you are able to make a decision that will benefit your current lifestyle. 

**Employee** 

1\. You are guaranteed to be paid and also you get a W2 at the end of the year. 

2\. You may be bound to set hours, scheduled breaks. There is not much flexibility.  
3\. You are able to obtain benefits to full-time and some part-time employees. 

4\. With employee positions you are able to get discounts or great incentives. 

5\. You are responsible for creating your home office according to their requirements. 

**Independent contractor** 

1\. You may get a 1099, but you are responsible for reporting your own federal and state taxes. 

2\. Some positions allow you to create your own hours or choose hours that works best for you. 

3\. You may need to pay out of pocket for your tests and checks, and other courses to be considered eligible to be chosen as a possible contractor to work for a particular client. 

4\. You are responsible for creating your home office according to their requirements. 

So it is really not which is better than the other, both have their pros and cons. It just depends on what you are looking for. Do you want to have your own business, your own hours, or more flexibility? An independent contractor arrangement may be the better solution for you. If you prefer your taxes to be prepared for you by a W2, you want a set schedule and you would like the possibility of getting the discounts or incentives, then being an employee may work best for you. It all boils down to your comfort zone and what may work best for your household.  
**Chapter 4** 

What do I have to invest? 

![][image5]  
So LaToya, I want to work from home, I want to be with my family, I want to do the things I want to do and be with my family. What if I’m not a millionaire, what if I do not have all this money to invest into myself or to get started with working from home? 

I’m so glad you asked\! First of all, working from home requires some type of investment \-- period. Investment could be taking your time out to apply for positions or to build your resume. You have to be prepared to invest in yourself. Do not look at it as investing in a business, but look at it as investing in yourself. Your reward will be greater in the end. 

Here are some instances where you may need to invest: 

1\. Be prepared to pay for a background check. Some companies want you to pay for your own background check. This may range from \$9.99-\$35. Why? Because when employers see that you have invested in yourself, it means that you are serious enough to be a candidate to work from home.  
2\. Independent contractors, be prepared to come out of pocket, not only for your background check, but your certification courses based upon a particular client. 

3\. Invest in your coach. Sometimes it’s good to hire an expert who has the experience and can assist you by encouraging you while providing you with the tools you need to get started. Don’t try and do it by yourself. 

4\. Invest in your success. If you are not prepared to present a quality resume, and/or cover letter, then hire an expert to create an effective resume package for you. 

If you are interested in starting your own virtual assistant business, then grab a pen and paper and be prepared to take notes as Regina Lewis talks about her personal journey in starting her own virtual assistant business later in this book.

**Chapter 6** 

Starting Your Own Virtual Assistant Business Regina Lewis 

I remember when I worked outside of the home. The endless days of waking the kids, while it was still dark, dressing and feeding them, rushing them off to daycare, running to catch the bus to work, arriving to work exhausted because I had already been up 3 hours, taking phone calls from the sitter because one of the kids was sick/ misbehaving/ just took their first step, typing, more phone calls, the boss asking at the last minute if I can stay for five more minutes to finish up but in the back of my mind I am screaming, “ No\! I have to pick my kids up at 6\!” Then it was the whole day in reverse: leave work, catch the bus, pick up the kids, try to catch the sitter on the days happening while they are all clamoring for my attention, go home, fix dinner/clean/catch the news, eat, play a bit, storytime, bath, tears because they don’t want to go to the sitter next day (“Can’t you just stay home with us”), cleaning, laundry, bed for kids, preparing for the next day, collapse. 

Are you tired? I sure was. 

The deciding moment to begin my work from home life was when the daycare provider became extremely unreliable and I actually began to fear for my children’s safety while they were in her care. Her son, the same age as one of my boys, was extremely unruly and my boys were beginning to exhibit some bad habits. This coupled with the exhausted treadmill I was on made me realize something had to change. Quickly\! 

I prayed and took my first leap of faith. Not knowing how my boss was going to receive what I was about to tell her (and frankly at this point, I just didn’t care), I was determined to go into her office and tell her that I was going to have to resign. I felt torn between my domestic and office responsibilities. But my family came first.  
Well, I took a deep breath and laid out my dilemma. I told her I could not continue working with her. It was too stressful on me and my family and I just was not being productive at work. I gave her my notice. 

She looked at my note, looked at me and smiled. “Regina why didn’t you just tell me what was going on? I have a family too and understand the demands.” 

Wow, she understood. But her next words shocked me even more. “How about you just work from home?” 

HUH? I did not expect that one. I dreamed of a job where I can be at home and still produce an income but like so many others, I did not believe it could happen. I thought most ads were scams and had become so cynical, I looked at everything skeptically. This progressive-thinking woman opened the door to my virtual world. I haven’t looked back since. 

What is a virtual assistant? According to Virtual Networking Association (www\.vanetworking.com), a Virtual Assistant (VA) is a highly-trained independent entrepreneur who provides a myriad of business support services virtually via phone, fax and internet based on technology to support and meet the growing needs of businesses worldwide. 

My boss, Dee, was a successful real estate agent in a busy brokerage. At any given time, she had multiple listings on the market. She knew how to market her services to potential clients and how to close the deal, get them to sign the contract. Plus she owned a successful property management company overseeing several residential and commercial properties. Having a virtual assistant was great for her. 

The transition from office to home went smoothly. I already had a computer, fax machine and telephone so no extra equipment was needed. We transferred office phones to my phone during the day. After hours, I forwarded the phones to the after-hours answering machine. I was able to log into the office email from home and we both communicated that way throughout the day. Of course if it was great urgent matter, I just called her on her cellphone. We met every 2 weeks to review any projects and to issues if the arrangement was working.  
Did it work? YES\! 

It worked for several reasons: one, I wanted to work from home. My family needed me home but I needed to work. Two, Dee was a wonderful person who trusted me enough to basically put her business on the line without hesitation. 

It wasn’t all a day at the beach. It takes true organization and determination to work from home with kids. I talked to my boys and told them Mommy would be working from home. After they stopped cheering, I solemnly told them that although I would be working, there would be times were I would have to take a phone call, and type a contract. I needed their cooperation to make this work. 

Has it worked? Is it tough? YES\! But my kids are much happier now and so am I. I am able to take my kids to appointments without asking for time off. I can schedule family outings around our schedule. The savings on daycare have been astronomical. The cost of daycare and transportation was well over \$1000 per month. We had immediate savings just by me working from home\! If you are lucky like I was to convert an employer to a client, that’s great. But if that’s not the case and you are starting from scratch, where do you find clients? 

The following marketing techniques are the ones I have personally used to sign clients to retainer contracts. I highly advise you to try several ideas, track what does and what does not work and stick with it. You do not want to waste money on marketing strategies that are not effective. 

1\. If you are just starting out and not quite sure what services you want to offer clients, I recommend volunteering. I went online to www\.volunteermatch.org and found an organization in need of a virtual assistant. By working with this client, I not only got to hone my business skills but provide pro bono administrative support services to an organization in need. Many are more than open to volunteers. In addition to routine administrative tasks, you may want to offer to develop a website, come up with new fundraising ideas, create a donor database, newsletter submission; the ideas go on and on. 

2\. There are many freelance sites online. Keep in mind that you will not be able to demand your initial retainer rate but they are great to utilize when  
beginning your business. Some of the better known sites are: www\.odesk.com, www\.guru.com and www\.elance.com. Read all policy information carefully. You will need to know how to submit resumes and how/when you will get paid. 

3\. A free marketing to is your email signature. Create an email signature with all your contact information such as phone number, website and a tagline describing your business. I did sign a client this way. Our initial contact had nothing to do with my business but about finding a house. 

4\. Talk to EVERYONE about your business. You never know who knows who you need to know. During a meeting with a woman regarding a non business related matter, I casually brought up my business. It turns out she owns a nonprofit and was looking for administrative help. Had I not brought up my business she would have not known about my services and I would not have found out she needed help. A win/win situation. 

5\. Set up a Facebook business page and a blog. These two platforms are essential to your success. Include engaging content on both, something that will get your target audience talking. 

6\. Don’t want to deal with marketing and billing issues? Consider partnering with another virtual assistant. There are several companies that hire VA’s as subcontractors. 

Above all, decide early on your niche. Will you provide written content, like blog posts and press releases? Or are you a techie who loves to design websites? No one person can do everything and it’s best to be an expert in one area than mediocre in several areas.

101 Things You Can Do as a Virtual Assistant ***Specific Tasks*** 

1\) Process mailings for clients 

2\) Perform outbound telemarketing calls seeking clients/sellers/buyers 3\) Enter contacts into MS Outlook or other database management program 4\) Set/cancel appointments 

5\) Work with Excel spreadsheets to organize leads and other data 6\) Work with MS Word to create mail merges and process mailings 7\) Answer incoming calls 

8\) Return phone calls 

9\) Type and send letters or contracts 

10\) Make travel arrangements 

11\) Call for quotes for other services 

12\) Order services on the client’s behalf 

13\) Screen and answer emails 

14\) Prepare newsletters 

15\) Plan events or meetings 

16\) Arrange and put together seminars or teleseminars 

17\) Proof read your written materials 

18\) Transcribe meetings  
19\) Correspond with clients/tenants regarding payments and late fees, via mail and phone 

20\) Mail outs such as postcards or letters for marketing purposes 21\) Check voice mail; return calls 

22\) Photos (edit and list on websites) 

23\) Research 

24\) Flyers 

25\) Create PowerPoint presentations 

26\) Thank you notes 

27\) Newsletters 

28\) Customer call backs 

29\) Promotional mailing 

30\) Thank you gifts 

31\) Order promotional items 

***Secretarial Services*** 

32\) **Answer telephones during business hours.** Calls can be routed to your home office 

33\) Using new programs which allow remote access to computers, the virtual assistant can work on your computer at a distance. Running scans, repairing registries, **updating the system to run better and faster** all can be done remotely. Interactive software is commonly used to allow the virtual assistant and your calendar to be **on the same page**. 

34\) **Confirm appointments** for clients on a weekly basis. Your client can simply fax or email a list to you. You call the appointments and note who is  
confirmed and who must be rescheduled. Fax or email the list back to the clients and update the client calendar online. 

35\) Provide **directions** to a meeting or seminar. Get the directions and either calls or email those directions to the client. 

36\) Fill out **routine paperwork for clients.** 

37\) Keep **back-up tapes** of your client’s computer. They can send to you for safe-keeping. In the event of a disaster on your client’s computer, you will have the files\! 

38\) **Coordinate air travel**, car rental and hotel reservations. Take care of the arrangements and email the itinerary to your client. 

39\) Conduct **billing for your clients.** 

40\) A virtual assistant can **audit banking records**, and review telephone bills, including cell phone records and report any problems back to the clients. 

41\) Prepare business procedures and type business manuals. ***Research*** 

42\) **Research**. The virtual assistant contacts several hotels in the area to find availability of the date, size, and specifics of the seminar. Obtain **written quotes** from the hotels that can accommodate the request. Review each **quote** for completeness and report the findings for final decision. 

43\) **Obtain pricing for office equipment** and email the information to the client for the final decision. 

44\) **Research a topic online** for an important proposal. Do a keyword search and list the 

websites/findings to the client. 

45\) **Prepare a marketing plan,** contact possible advertising outlets on the Internet, magazines, periodicals, newspapers, etc. and acquire information **on pricing, publishing dates, publishing deadlines**, payment policies, etc. 

***Word Processing/Presentations***  
46\) Take notes at meetings and type them, formatting into a newsletter if needed. 

47\) **Edit and** format reports. 

48\) Type and print **the same letter personalized to many recipients. Mail the letter and charge the postage costs back to the client.** 

49\) Prepare a PowerPoint presentation for a client **seminar.** 

50\) Prepare a questionnaire fact sheet for seminar participants. Follow up with participants and **summarize the questionnaire responses** in a report. 

51\) Better still – design the questionnaire 

52\) **Create a form** or template for your client. 

53\) Verify client database (**name**, spelling, title and address). Save the database as a “zip” file and email to the client. 

54\) Send out **email blasts, using ConstantContact.** 

55\) Be available via Instant Message to handle **last minute projects** effectively. 

56\) **Send out monthly reports** for customers. Keep a calendar and sends reports in a timely manner. 

***Desktop Publishing*** 

57\) Design, type and print **brochures** for a client’s business. 

58\) Submit the design file to a professional print shop and simply email the file to the shop for printing. 

59\) **Update** your client’s blog. Get ideas from your client or think of your own. 

60\) Conduct an **eBay auction**. Set up the auction, upload photos, monitor and complete the sale for your client. 

61\) Design **business cards**. 

62\) Design **schedules, calendars or flyers.**  
63\) Design a custom website or blog, maintain it on a regular basis, adding current articles or information as needed. 

64\) **Set-up an autoresponder** using AWeber or MailChimp. 

65\) **Design and prepare the newsletters**, and arrange printing and mailing, or emailing, on schedule. 

66\) **Create postcards to be sent to your client’s customers. Order** from the fulfillment house for delivery in bulk to your office, her/his office, or to be labeled and sent out directly. 

67\) **Send a blind survey to a focus group** or list of former customers for feedback. 

68\) Contact old customers via phone with a **prepared script** or by sending a **targeted mailing**. 

***Transcription Services*** 

69\) **Record calls and transcribe the tape** for clients. 

70\) Your client sends you an MP3 file. Transcribe the audio and email the completed transcript back to the client. 

***Email Services*** 

71\) Set up a general email account (info@mycompany.com). **Retrieve all email, sort, respond** to routine requests, and forward items of importance to your client. 

72\) Monitor email while your client is on vacation or out of the office. **Contact the client** with urgent messages or respond on their behalf. 

73\) Manage your client’s **eZine/newsletter**. Although many features can be automated, correct any incorrect subscription requests or undeliverable email messages. 

***Telephone/Fax Services***  
74\) Record a voicemail for your client if they will be on vacation and monitor incoming calls. Customers may contact your directly as well. 

75\) Have your client forward their calls to you so you may answer them live. Respond to routine requests, and contact your client with urgent messages. 

76\) **Retrieve messages from voice mail** and respond to routine requests. 

77\) When planning a seminar or conference **make phone calls to key contacts**, give a brief overview of the seminar, and schedule a phone appointment for your client to connect with the contact personally. 

***Internet Services*** 

78\) Upload **photographs online** through a service or by creating a 

personal page (Flickr, for example). Scan and resize the photos, then send out an invitation to a designated email list to access the photographs. 

79\) Perform searches to **locate a hard to find item**. 

80\) Make **changes to a client’s website**. 

81\) **Promote your client’s website** by submitting the URL, key words and description to various search engines on a routine basis. 

82\) **Increase the number** of subscribers to your client’s electronic newsletter by **listing the newsletter with a variety of online directories** and follow up to make sure the listings are accurate. 

83\) Contact other list owners to inquire about mutual cross promotion. 

84\) **Submit articles** written by you or your client to eZines to **increase exposure.** 

85\) Monitor banner ad placements/click thrus and make recommendations for 

adjustments. 

86\) Set up a shopping cart to sell products and monitor sales reports.  
87\) **Contact similar websites to your client’s** and request mutual link exchange. 

88\) **Periodically review your client’s website** and verify links. Fix broken links. 

***Bookkeeping*** 

89\) Your client needs **bill paying services**. Use on-line bill payment services. Security features can be set up which make this a safe and simple solution. 

90\) You client needs **bill paying services plus data entry into accounting software.** 

**You** can: 

a. Set up a checking account with payment authorization for both of you. As the bills are prepared for payment, notify your client how much money to deposit into the account. 

b. Prepare the checks for payment and mail back to your client for signature and mailing. 

c. If available from your bank, use on-line bill payment services. As bills are paid, enter the transactions into accounting software. In addition, reconcile bank statements, enter credit card transactions, prepare invoices, make and/or enter deposits, and prepare end of month reports. 

91\) **Collect on past due invoices**, make payment arrangements, accept credit cards over the phone, etc. 

92\) Your client needs monthly bank reconciliation. Using the check register and the bank statement, **enter all data into accounting software** and reconcile the account. The accounting file is sent back to your via email attachment. 

93\) **Remind your client, via email** or telephone, when billing due dates arrive.  
94\) Your client needs monthly **auditing of accounts** payable and receivable, especially if these services are performed by an on-site employee. 

95\) Prepare income tax returns for your client’s business. Prepare 1099’s and W-2s to be sent out to vendors and contractors. 

***Purchasing Services*** 

96\) **Order supplies for your client** and have them delivered directly to your client’s office or home. 

97\) Research the various makes, models, etc., of office equipment and have written quotes sent to you. Purchase and arrange for delivery. 

98\) Set up lines of credit with vendors and monitor to **keep your client’s credit information current** and accurate. 

99\) **Order marketing materials** (stationery, brochures, envelopes, etc.) for your client. Obtain pricing quotes; coordinate ordering, design, quantity, delivery and payment. 

100\) Keep track of birthdays and other milestones, research appropriate gifts, suggest those items for approval, and coordinate the purchase and delivery of same. 

101\) **Keep track of birthdays and send out cards** for your clients. 

***Writing/Editing Services*** 

102\) **Write, edit and proofread** marketing literature. 

103\) Type, format, proofread, edit, spell check, and grammar check documents. 

104\) Write articles on your client’s behalf. 

***Marketing Services***  
105\) Implement **an advertising plan or promo.** Monitor the plan, submit ads by deadlines, track expiration dates, coordinate payment, handle correspondence with advertising vendors, and continually update the advertising report and/or advertising budget report. 

106\) **Monitor customer satisfaction** by creating a feedback questionnaire or survey, email to customers, review the responses and summarize the responses. 

107\) Prepare a **welcome package** and send it to your client’s new customer. 

108\) Set up lunch appointments for your client to meet with potential customers. 

109\) Set up exhibits at conventions or expos on a regular basis. 

***Personal Services*** 

110\) Schedule personal tasks such as car maintenance, order groceries or make flight arrangements. 

111\) **Keep your client’s calendar** and remind them of dentist/client/significant other appointments, family appointments, classes to take, or project deadlines. 

112\) Research personal items, such as summer camps, schools, etc., for clients. 

113\) Plan **a wedding/reunion/backyard barbeque**, assist with the invitation list, mail the invitations, track RSVPs, track gifts received and even send thank you cards. 

114\) **Research and recommend life insurance, car insurance, home owners insurance, etc.** 

115\) **Plan vacations,** provide your client with options, and then make the travel arrangements, such as air, hotel and car rental, or all-inclusive resorts or cruise comparisons. 

116\) Help a motivational speaker **promote their speaking career**. Make appointments with organizations to arrange speaking engagements, send out  
materials, follow up with inquiries, and **coordinate public relations** such as press releases. 

117\) Provide **daily updating** on personal investments, stocks, etc. 

118\) Work with an author to assist them in **writing a book**. Compile rough drafts, notes, fragments, letters or memoirs and get them into an editable form to begin the process of formatting the book, research publishers, and send out queries. 

119\) Upload **audio files** to a website or set up to be downloaded as a **free report**. 

Can you think of more? **Great\! Go for it\!** 

There are lots of business owners who need you and your services\! Good luck to you\!  
**Chapter 8** 

**Pre-Interview Sessions are helpful** 

Conducting pre interview sessions can be helpful for you in the long run. It helps prepare you for the “Big Day” and eases your nerves a little bit. If you have never interviewed for a job before you must know that not every company hires the first person that applies to their job posting. You have to know how to sell yourself well and make your resume and character stand out from the rest. Pre-Interview sessions are very rewarding and beneficial to those who are new to the workforce. If you are unsure on how to get started and you want some practice make sure to reach out to me on my website www\.virtuallynsync.net and I will definitely set up a time where we can go over some of the most common interview questions that employers ask during the interview. I have listed 10 of the most common interview question so that you are able to get an idea on what to expect during your typical pre-interview session with me. 

1\. Tell me about yourself 

2\. Tell me about your past work experience. 

3\. What do you know about our company? 

4\. Tell me about a time when……. 

5\. Why should we choose you? 

6\. What questions do you have for me? (Always Always asks questions) 

7\. What are your greatest strengths? 

8\. What did you like or dislike about your previous job? 

9\. Why do you want to change jobs? 

10\. How would you handle an irate customer?  
These are just a few questions but depending on the employer the questions may be worded differently. However, if you practice answering the questions before the interview you will become more comfortable answering these same questions in the future.  
**Chapter 9** 

**Mystery Shopping Opportunities** 

**![][image7]**  
If you are not comfortable with working in a call center and/or you would still like to work outside the home; you can always try out the joy of mystery shopping. 

Mystery shopping is the process of measuring and recording specific elements of the customer experience through the use of pre-recruited and qualified consumers (typically independent contractors) who serve as mystery shoppers. (Mystery Shopping Provider Association) 

A mystery shopper is a person who visits an establishment (typically a retail store, bank, restaurant or other such places where the public does business) for the purpose of observing and measuring customer service, product quality and the environment of the establishment in general. (Mystery Shopping Provider Association) 

You are given specific instructions on what the company is looking for and you are required to write down your observations during your visit to that specific site. Some shopping assignments require you to make a phone call,  
while others require an in-store visit. You are basically your own boss and you responsible for submitting your observations and proof of purchase (if necessary) to the company in order to get compensated for your time. Becoming a mystery shopper is very rewarding as it allows you the flexibility of choosing what assignment works for you. One of the places that I started at was the Mystery Shopping Provider Association. This association provides you with the companies that are looking for people like you to become their eye. I have listed a few of the companies that I have found to be legit below. 

1\. Mystery Shopping Provider Association- http\://mysteryshop.org 2\. BestMark \-www\.bestmark.com 

3\. Monterery Mystery Shopping- www\.montereymysteryshopping.com 4\. Jancyn-Prophet- www\.shoppers.jancyn.com 

You definitely want to start with the MSPA because they will definitely send on the right path and provide you with nothing but the best there is to offer\!
